suppressions.candidate: Legacy staff records could lose their identity, credential, or decision reference while roles are introduced.
suppressions.note: The migration only adds role and ativo columns, backfills role on existing rows, then constrains role. It neither recreates admin_users nor touches applications.decided_by, so IDs, email/password_hash values, and existing foreign-key references remain intact.

suppressions.candidate: Concurrent or repeated issued-document rows could lack database protection for version identity and current-version reads.
suppressions.note: The migration creates the unique application/kind/version index and the application/kind/version DESC index required to reject duplicate versions and support latest-version queries; the application-row locking policy belongs to the issuance service rather than migration DDL.

suppressions.candidate: New observation or issued-document rows could be orphaned or survive deletion of their application.
suppressions.note: Both application foreign keys are required and use ON DELETE CASCADE. Author and issuer foreign keys use ON DELETE RESTRICT, preserving attributable records by preventing staff-account deletion while referenced.

suppressions.candidate: The database could accept an issued-document MIME type other than application/pdf.
suppressions.note: The schema gives mime_type a non-null application/pdf default and the sole issuance service sets that literal. The task's explicit database-enforced invariants are kind, positive version/size, uniqueness, and foreign keys; no concrete path in the selected code supplies a caller-controlled MIME type.
